"Measuring AI ability to complete long tasks" METR March 2025

sources_considered.why: Read dated results and methodology passages. Independent pre-release evaluation of o3 using agent interfaces without o3-specific adaptation.
Read the original paper's Claude results and limitations. Provides success-rate measurements for Claude 3.7 Sonnet.
Read model and methodology passages. The Apple experiments use o3-mini rather than o3 and therefore cannot establish both named-model comparisons.
Read the methodological critique and successful Hanoi demonstrations. These limit conclusions from Apple's setup but do not overturn the broader task-completion measurements.

evidence_items.explanation: The evaluated o3 checkpoint reached only 50% predicted success at tasks taking humans about 1.5 hours, despite setting a new high in this evaluation. This supports caution about dependable complex-task completion, while the pre-release checkpoint and agent interface limit direct application to unassisted released o3.

evidence_items.locator: Section 4.2.1, Time horizons at 50% success rate vs 80% success rate
evidence_items.explanation: The section reports Claude 3.7 Sonnet's approximately 59-minute horizon at 50% success and approximately 15-minute horizon at 80% success. These substantial failure rates support the reliability warning for that Claude version.

unresolved_gaps: The tests use agent scaffolds, not exclusively unassisted chat.
The o3 evaluation uses pre-release checkpoints.
The Claude evidence concerns 3.7 Sonnet and does not establish the same quantitative results for every Claude version.
Exact test dates are not reported; event months reflect the dated contemporary evaluations.
